assets/annotations/korean_honggildong_l1.title: 1. 길동의 고민
assets/annotations/korean_honggildong_l1.text: 길동의 아버지는 나라의 중요한 일을 했습니다. 어머니는 그 집에서 일하는 사람이었습니다. 하지만 어머니는 아버지의 아내가 아니었습니다. 그래서 아버지는 길동이 아버지를 “아버지”라고 부르지 못하게 했습니다. 길동은 형을 “형”이라고 부를 수도 없었습니다. 길동은 마음이 매우 아프고 슬펐습니다.

entries.explanation_en: After a time expression, 에 says when something happens.
Marks the noun that is the subject of a statement.
Sets up the noun that the rest of the statement is about; it can also signal contrast.
Connects a noun to another noun it owns or is related to.
Marks the noun affected by the verb.
Follows a name before a noun to say what that person or thing is called.
Marks the name or words used with a verb such as ‘call’ or ‘say’.
Places the action or state before now. The written form changes with the preceding stem.
Ends a statement in a formal, polite style.
Turns a descriptive word into a modifier placed before its noun.
After an action verb, this form describes a noun by an action already completed.
Forms a modifier for an action considered possible or expected; before 수 it helps express ability or possibility.
Connects a noun to what someone or something is. It can take past and polite endings.
A verb in its -(으)ㄹ modifier form followed by 수 없다 means that doing it is not possible.
Attach 에서 to a place noun to mark where an action takes place. The same form follows nouns ending in a consonant or a vowel.
Attach 도 to a noun to mean ‘also’ or ‘too’. With emphasis, it can mean ‘even’. It usually replaces a subject, topic, or object marker, but can follow other particles.

Attach -게 to a verb or descriptive stem and follow it with 하다. The construction means to make or let someone perform an action, or to cause a state. When the action is negative, it can express preventing someone from doing something.

Attach -고 to a verb or descriptive stem to connect it to another action or description, often meaning ‘and’. The final predicate can supply the tense for both connected parts when they share the same time.
Before 아니다, mark the noun naming what someone or something is not with 이 after a consonant or 가 after a vowel. This noun gives the identity or category being denied.
Attach -지 to a verb stem and follow it with 못하다 to express inability to perform the action. The inability may come from lack of skill or from circumstances that prevent the action.

Attach -는 to an action verb stem and place the resulting modifier before a noun. Drop a stem-final ㄹ before adding -는. The modifier describes an ongoing or habitual action associated with the noun. Its time is understood relative to the main statement, so it can describe an action taking place at a past time.

occurrences.context_en: 의 connects Gildong to his father: ‘Gildong’s father’. 길동 is the reviewed shortened name of 홍길동.
occurrences.sentence: 길동의 아버지는 나라의 중요한 일을 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 는 sets Gildong’s father as the topic: the sentence tells us what work he did.
occurrences.sentence: 길동의 아버지는 나라의 중요한 일을 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 의 connects the country to its important work, referring here to work for the country.
occurrences.sentence: 길동의 아버지는 나라의 중요한 일을 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 중요한 describes the following noun 일: ‘important work’. This is a descriptive modifier, not a completed action.
occurrences.sentence: 길동의 아버지는 나라의 중요한 일을 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 을 marks 일 as the work that his father did.
occurrences.sentence: 길동의 아버지는 나라의 중요한 일을 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 하다 becomes 했다 in the past; 하였 contracts to 했. His father did this work before the time of narration.
occurrences.sentence: 길동의 아버지는 나라의 중요한 일을 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 했습니다 presents the past action ‘did’ in the narrator’s formal polite style.
occurrences.sentence: 길동의 아버지는 나라의 중요한 일을 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 는 makes Gildong's mother the topic: the sentence explains her role in the household.
에서 marks the household as the place where his mother worked.
일하는 modifies 사람: a person who works. The modifier describes her work at the time of the past-tense statement, so the natural English translation is 'who worked.'
이다 connects his mother with 사람이, identifying her as a person who worked in that household; 이 here belongs to the copula, not a subject particle.
었 places her role as a household worker in the past.
습니다 ends the statement about his mother's former role in a formal, polite style.
는 sets his mother as the topic: the sentence explains her relationship to his father.
의 connects 아버지 to 아내: ‘his father's wife.’
가 marks 아내 as the role denied by 아니다: his mother was not his father's wife.
The past form 아니었다 places the statement about her status in the past.
-습니다 ends 아니었습니다 as a formal polite statement; the meaning remains ‘was not.’
는 makes Gildong's father the topic: the following statement describes what he imposed.
occurrences.sentence: 그래서 아버지는 길동이 아버지를 “아버지”라고 부르지 못하게 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 이 marks Gildong as the subject of the embedded action of calling his father by a title.
occurrences.sentence: 그래서 아버지는 길동이 아버지를 “아버지”라고 부르지 못하게 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 를 marks the father as the person Gildong would address.
occurrences.sentence: 그래서 아버지는 길동이 아버지를 “아버지”라고 부르지 못하게 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 라고 marks “아버지” as the exact title used in addressing his father.
occurrences.sentence: 그래서 아버지는 길동이 아버지를 “아버지”라고 부르지 못하게 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 부르지 connects to 못하다 to express inability to call. Here that inability is imposed by the father.
occurrences.sentence: 그래서 아버지는 길동이 아버지를 “아버지”라고 부르지 못하게 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: The entire construction says that the father prevented Gildong from using the title. The past tense belongs to 했습니다.
occurrences.sentence: 그래서 아버지는 길동이 아버지를 “아버지”라고 부르지 못하게 했습니다.
occurrences.display_meaning_en: prevented him from calling him that

occurrences.context_en: 못하게 states the inability that the following 했습니다 causes: the father makes it so that Gildong cannot use the title.
occurrences.sentence: 그래서 아버지는 길동이 아버지를 “아버지”라고 부르지 못하게 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 했- places the father's act of preventing the use of the title in the past.
occurrences.sentence: 그래서 아버지는 길동이 아버지를 “아버지”라고 부르지 못하게 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: -습니다 ends the narration in a formal polite style.
occurrences.sentence: 그래서 아버지는 길동이 아버지를 “아버지”라고 부르지 못하게 했습니다.

occurrences.context_en: 은 makes Gildong the topic: the sentence explains another restriction he faced.
을 marks his older brother as the person Gildong could not address by the quoted family title.
이라고 marks “형” as the title used with 부르다, ‘call someone by a name or title.’
부르다 becomes 부를 before 수, presenting calling him that as a possible action rather than stating that it happened.
부를 수 없었습니다 says Gildong could not call him that; 도 adds ‘even,’ emphasizing that this family title was forbidden too.
occurrences.display_meaning_en: could not even call him that

occurrences.context_en: 도 attaches to 수 and emphasizes that even the possibility of addressing his older brother as ‘older brother’ was unavailable.
없다 becomes 없었다, placing the lack of permission or possibility in the past.
없었습니다 presents the past state in the passage’s formal polite narrative style.
은 sets Gildong as the topic: the sentence describes how he felt.
이 marks 마음 as the subject. 마음이 아프다 describes emotional pain: Gildong felt hurt.
-고 connects feeling hurt with being sad. The past ending on 슬펐습니다 places both feelings in the past.
슬프다 becomes 슬펐다 with -었-, expressing that Gildong was sad.
-습니다 gives the past statement 슬펐습니다 its formal polite ending.

forms.label: Connective form before 못하다
forms.meaning_en: call, linked to the following expression of inability

forms.label: Result-state connective in -게 하다
forms.meaning_en: so that he could not do so

forms.label: Prospective modifier before 수
forms.meaning_en: call (an action whose possibility is being considered)
